2.  This criminal revision has been filed challenging the order dated 19.02.2024 passed in Cr. Appeal (Juvenile) No. 08 of 2024 by learned Additional Sessions Judge - I -cum Children's Court,
Hazaribag whereby the appeal of the petitioner challenging refusal to grant bail has been dismissed.
The prayer of the petitioner for grant of bail has been rejected by the Court of learned Principal Magistrate, J.J. Board, Hazaribagh in connection with Korrah P.S. Case No. 321 of 2023 registered under Section 420, 385, 468, 471 /34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 66C/67 / 67 A of the Information Technology Act.
3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since 08.12.2023 in connection with the alleged offence and is 17 years of age.
She submits that the petitioner is a student and he lastly appeared in the examination of 11th class.
4. Learned counsel submits that the petitioner has no other criminal case against him other than the present and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.

As per the allegation, the petitioner Sajan Kumar @ Sajan Kumar Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ... Opposite ... on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116772742/
1 was found in association with a group of persons while committing the alleged crime.

entities.text: Sajan Kumar @ Sajan Kumar Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further submits that the Social Investigation Report has been considered wherein it was observed that there is a likelihood that the petitioner would associate himself in bad company.

5. Learned counsel on instruction received from the uncle of the petitioner submits that the petitioner is willing to undertake skill development course in the form of Computer course in Talley / accounting.

She further submits that the father of the petitioner shall take appropriate care to ensure that the petitioner does not indulge in anti-social activities and keep the petitioner away from association of bad company and in such circumstances, the petitioner be released on bail.
6. Learned counsel for the Opposite Party opposes the prayer of the petitioner and submits that the impugned orders are well reasoned order.
However, the learned counsel submits that if the father of the petitioner is ready to take appropriate care of the petitioner, then an opportunity be granted to the petitioner.
He further submits that the report of the Probation Officer of the concerned district be placed before the Juvenile Justice Board from time to time to monitor the well-being of the petitioner.

7. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court is of the considered view that the petitioner being a student should be given an opportunity to improve himself.

The father of the petitioner has undertaken and the petitioner has also expressed his willingness to engage himself in additional learning of computer course in Talley / accounting and it has been submitted that the father of the petitioner is already running a small business and the skill so acquired by the petitioner could be of use in the running business of his father.
Further, the petitioner has already remained in custody since 08.12.2023.

The order refusing bail was passed by the learned Juvenile Justice Board way back on 18.01.2024 and now much time has elapsed and considering the custody of the petitioner and the aforesaid submissions this court is of the considered view that the petitioner be released and his activities be properly monitored by the probation officer of the district.
8.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this court is inclined to release the petitioner on bail and accordingly the impugned orders refusing to grant bail to the petitioner are hereby set aside.

9. Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.
25,000/- (Rs. Twenty-Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Juvenile Justice Board, Hazaribagh in connection with Korrah P.S. Case No. 321 of 2023 registered under Section 420, 385, 468, 471/34 of the Indian Penal Code and 66C/ 67/ 67A of the Information Technology Act, subject to the following conditions: -
(i). One of the bailors should be the father of the petitioner and the other one should be a close relative of the petitioner.
(ii). The father of the petitioner shall ensure that the petitioner forthwith takes admission in an appropriate institute for attending computer course in Talley /

Sajan Kumar @ Sajan Kumar Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ... Opposite ... on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116772742/
2 accounting.

entities.text: Sajan Kumar @ Sajan Kumar Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The father of the petitioner shall also ensure that the petitioner does not fall in bad company again.
(iii).

The Probation Officer of the District is directed to furnish the Social Investigation Report of the petitioner before the learned Juvenile Justice Board,
Hazaribagh in interval of every three months and the first report be submitted on or before 26th September 2024.
10.
Accordingly, with the above observations, this Criminal Revision is disposed of.

11. Let a copy of this order be communicated to the concerned Court/Juvenile Justice Board through e-mail/ 'FAX'.
